## 41ea3019baeb

**Reproduced teaching shortcut: randomly placed mirrors are usually irrelevant.**

At generator SHA-256
`3d86a1a2fd181863b33e94a817f7397dc5e4ca382d6bac1d19e1550468227ad4`,
I sampled 100 default inputs per band with seeds
`50000 + 10000*band_index + index` and `sample_index=index`. No emitted ray
touched any color-5/6/7 mirror in 88/100 easy, 88/100 medium, and 80/100 hard
inputs (256/300 total). Only 2/100 hard inputs and 0/100 easy/medium inputs
exercised at least two mirror interactions, despite the canonical task being a
two-reflection beam maze. All 300 sampled inputs passed `self_check`.

A complete four-sample easy window (`seed=1000`, sample indexes 0–3) is exactly
matched by the wrong rival “paint straight right through zero cells until a
nonzero cell or boundary; never turn.” The authoritative Racket outputs equal
that rival on all four inputs. A canonical input retained in the same evidence
differs from the rival, proving the rival is not equivalent to the intended
rule. See `checks/audit/41ea3019baeb/counterexample.json`, with supported Racket
receipts in `racket.json`, `lesson-racket.json`, and `canonical-racket.json`.

The generated witnesses pass the target validator and belong to its documented
default domain. This audit target was not modified.

## 41ea3019baeb

**Reproduced teaching shortcut.** The generator usually places color-6/7 mirrors
where no emitted beam ever reaches them. A rival that paints straight right from
each color-2 emitter through zeroes and treats every nonzero cell as a blocker
therefore ignores mirror turning entirely.

On 100 accepted draws per band (generator SHA-256
`3d86a1a2fd181863b33e94a817f7397dc5e4ca382d6bac1d19e1550468227ad4`),
zero mirror interactions occurred in 88/100 easy, 88/100 medium, and 80/100 hard
draws; at least two interactions occurred only 0/100, 0/100, and 2/100. The exact
easy lesson at seed `1000`, sample indices `0..3`, contains zero interactions in
all four accepted inputs. The authoritative Racket rule (`2aaa46b96280`) matches
the straight-right rival on all four, while the same rival differs from a
canonical input on 10 cells. Evidence: `checks/audit/41ea3019baeb/probe.json`,
`lesson-racket.json`, `canonical-racket.json`, and `counterexample.json`.

Suggested repair: schedule lessons with guaranteed reachable mirror interactions,
including at least one two-mirror/turn sequence, and declare the straight-right
rule as a lesson competitor. I did not edit this audit target.

## 41ea3019baeb

**Classification: reproduced in-domain teaching shortcut.** The audited source SHA-256 is `3d86a1a2fd181863b33e94a817f7397dc5e4ca382d6bac1d19e1550468227ad4`. The combined audit found no task-local tests and the strict semantic gate failed because no semantic contract is declared (`checks/audit/41ea3019baeb-combined/result.json`).

Across 100 samples per band, 88 easy, 88 medium, and 80 hard paths touched no mirror; zero easy/medium and only two hard paths touched at least two mirrors (`checks/audit/41ea3019baeb/mirror-probe.json`). More decisively, the four lawful generated inputs from seed 1000, sample indices 0–3, are all matched by a `straight-right-no-turn` rival. The canonical task refutes that rival, so the generated lesson can teach a shortcut that does not solve the intended reflection rule (`checks/audit/41ea3019baeb/comparison.json`).

The exact generated lesson, rival labels, authoritative Racket labels, canonical counterexample, and probe are retained under `checks/audit/41ea3019baeb/`. This is an audit finding only; the assigned audit source was not modified.
